evidence.note: d-embed-accounts: accounts are read alone by account number (hot, fund transfer and utility payment resolve both legs via findByNumber, never through the user) so they stay a separate collection keyed by their own _id with userId as a reference

d-embed-accounts: balances are updated per transfer on the account row alone, independent of the user document; the fixture fan-out (user->account 2/3/5 of 4 users) says nothing about production and an embedded array would be rewritten on every transfer

d-embed-transactions: transactions are append-only and unbounded (two rows per fund transfer sharing one transactionId, one per utility payment, never read back in core-banking); an embedded array under the account would grow without bound, so transactions stay a separate collection with accountId as a reference

d-embed-transactions: JPA declares @OneToOne but the DDL FK account_id carries a non-unique KEY (V1.0.20210429210839__create_transaction_table.sql:11) and the service inserts many rows per account, so the entity cardinality is not trusted; the fixture has 0 transactions (data_profile fanout account->transaction unmeasured, d-profile-outlier = no seeding) so the proposer had no data for this edge

hot lookup by account number returns Optional (at most one row); the source DDL has no UNIQUE on number, the fixture's 14 numbers are distinct, the target index is declared unique per the ticket's index plan

warm lookup by identification number returns Optional (at most one row); the source DDL has no UNIQUE on identification_number, the fixture's 4 values are distinct, the target index is declared unique per the ticket's index plan

the proposer skips cold patterns in _index_plan, so this index is added by decision per the ticket's index plan; not declared unique because the ticket's plan does not call for it and the source has no UNIQUE on provider_name
reference-side index on the account FK, kept from the proposer's origin=reference entry and backed by the non-unique source KEY; production reads transactions by account and date range

reference_data_candidate disposition: banking_core_utility_account is a seed-only provider directory (6 rows, no FK in or out, read by id and by provider_name, never written by the application); labelled reference_data, kept as its own collection with numeric _id so UtilityPaymentRequest.providerId keeps resolving

resolution: excluded: mmp_fixture_meta is the plugin's own mysql-init.sh readiness marker (initialized_at, scripts_failed; no PK; 0 rows), not customer data and not one of the 4 in-scope core-banking tables. It must not be loaded, indexed or reconciled; model_patch.py has no op that removes a collection, so the mmpFixtureMeta entry stays in the spec with an empty key and this resolution, and the unit-migration / recon steps skip it (see 05_decisions.md s2.1-census entry 1 and s2.3 X10).

evidence.note: known incompatibility: the fixture-independent DDL has no UNIQUE on banking_core_account.number (only the PK and the user_id KEY), so the target unique index is stricter than the source. Kept unique on purpose: BankAccountRepository.findByNumber (repository/BankAccountRepository.java:10) returns Optional<> and treats number as a key lookup. Load policy: a duplicate number in a real export must FAIL the createIndex/load visibly (surfaced in the ticket), never be deduplicated or hidden.

Kept unique on purpose: UserRepository.findByIdentificationNumber (repository/UserRepository.java:10) returns Optional<> and treats it as a key lookup. Load policy: a duplicate identification_number in a real export must FAIL the createIndex/load visibly, never be deduplicated or hidden.

MySQL 8 default collation utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci (case-insensitive): the DDL declares no CHARSET/COLLATE and the census does not capture collation_name. Selected d-collation: create this index with collation {locale: 'en', strength: 2} so lookups keep MySQL semantics, and apply collation_casefold in recon to this field only. NOT machine-expressible: the spec's index schema carries keys+unique only (model_patch._index, recon config._index_spec) and field rules cannot be added by a decision op; this note is the only carrier -> app/index-creation constraint handed to s4.1.b01 (see 05_decisions.md s3.2 entry 3).
